rocke_bench__gpt_oss_sink_prefill_shapes: graph_match declines sink_token_tensor_uid. THE BLOCKER IS VERIFICATION, NOT ABI: IRunnableKernel::launch is a variadic template sizing its kernarg array from sizeof...(Args) (compilation/IRunnableKernel.hpp), so there is no five-argument ceiling -- passing sink_ptr is one more findDeviceBuffer plus one more launch argument. What actually blocks it is that the GPU reference executor, the one this engine's pinned CI target uses (REFERENCE_EXECUTOR gpu), declines sinks alongside block-sparse (GpuSdpaFwdPlan.hpp), so a shipped sink variant would have nothing in CI to check it against. The test_sdk CPU reference DOES compute sinks (CpuFpReferenceSdpa.hpp). rocKE serves these shapes and they ARE numerically verifiable -- just not by the executor this engine's CI is pinned to. Serving them is a bounded, four-part change: lift this decline, lift the use_sinks guard in kernelMatches, pass the sixth kernarg, and add a cpu-pinned integration target. This is a REPORTED coverage gap, not a scope cut.
